issues.problem: The YAML specifies a 3% tolerance, whereas the applicant-facing text states an absolute 18,000-word limit with excess text disregarded. These describe different enforcement boundaries; 3% corresponds to 540 words.
issues.fix: Set tolerance to zero, or explicitly describe the same tolerance and its enforcement in call.md.

issues.where: call.md and call.yaml: EO1 and SC1
issues.problem: EO1 requires adoption for routing, stock rotation and cold-chain interventions across three operator groups, while SC1 presents those functions as alternatives. It is unclear whether a project addressing only one function and operator group can satisfy the required outcomes.
issues.fix: Specify that EO1 concerns one or more selected logistics functions and relevant operator groups, or explicitly require all listed functions and groups throughout the scope.

issues.problem: “Better prepared” has no observable completion condition, and the item combines readiness for NIS2 obligations with application of AI Act principles. A general statement about regulatory awareness could satisfy its wording without demonstrating either result.
issues.fix: Separate the two outcomes and specify an assessable result for each, such as an operator-tested cybersecurity responsibility and risk-management procedure addressing applicable NIS2 requirements, and a documented assessment of accuracy, robustness, cybersecurity and human oversight.

issues.problem: SC3 combines two independently satisfiable requirements: comparative evaluation and public release of a benchmark. A proposal could complete either without completing the other, making this an unsuitable single checkable item.
issues.fix: Split SC3 into a comparative-evaluation requirement and a separate requirement to release the test scenarios as an open benchmark, subject to ME4.

issues.where: call.md: Specific conditions; call.yaml: ME2 and eligibility
issues.problem: ME2 mixes a narrative requirement concerning consortium expertise with a consortium-composition eligibility condition requiring an operator participant. The latter belongs in eligibility rather than inside a mandatory narrative element.
issues.fix: Move the operator-participation condition into the eligibility provisions in both files. Retain a narrative requirement to demonstrate the computing, food-domain and operational expertise and explain access to the demonstrator.

issues.where: call.md and call.yaml: ME5; call.md: Part B sections 3.1 and 3.2
issues.problem: ME5 repeats the template requirements to state the requested contribution, describe participant roles and provide person-month allocations. Its additional requirement for costs per participant and work package is embedded among these repeated demands.
issues.fix: Limit ME5 to the additional requirement: provide costs by participant and work package that reconcile with the requested EU contribution. Leave participant roles, the contribution statement and staff effort to the existing template requirements.
